name: Create onboarding tasks from a Google Sheets hire list with due dates based on start date

parameters.content:
## Create onboarding tasks from a hire list

Runs once each morning and reads a shared Google Sheet that HR maintains. Only rows marked approved with a start date become tasks.

For each hire the workflow builds tasks for management, department, IT and equipment, each with a due date derived from the start date and a named owner. Only tasks whose due date is TODAY are sent (date computed in Europe/Berlin), so no task repeats daily. Owners get one email per task; incomplete rows go back to HR.

If the start date moves, the task is simply sent on the new due date — nothing ever fires on the old one. Generic example, no client data.

### 1. Daily trigger
One run each morning. Keep it small and idempotent: re-running only re-derives what the sheet says.

### 2. Hire list (Google Sheets)
Expects columns: name, start_date (YYYY-MM-DD), department, status. Sheets replaces the item data, so the Set node after it carries both the row and the config values forward.

### 3. Onboarding config + task builder (Set + Code)
Owners per team and the day offsets live in the Set node. The Code node emits one item per task that is due today (today computed in Europe/Berlin): team, owner, due date (start date minus offset), hire name and a short description. Config values are copied into each output item so later nodes never fall back to placeholders. An offset of 0 skips that team.

### 4. Notify owners
One email per task, addressed to the mapped owner, subject carries hire and due date. Values come straight from the task item.

### 5. HR review path
Approved rows that are incomplete (missing start date or name) are collected into one email to the HR inbox (hrInbox, not an owner address). This email repeats every morning until the row is fixed. The log node after the owner emails reads its values from the Build Onboarding Tasks node, because Send Email replaces the item data.

### Error path
Sheets and SMTP nodes use "On Error: Continue (using error output)" — except Alert Admin on Error, which continues on its regular output. Errors meet in Log Error, which mails the admin. The admin address is set directly in the Alert Admin node — on purpose, because when the Sheets read fails before the config node ran, its values are not reachable. In addition, a separate workflow with an Error Trigger can be registered under this workflow's Settings → Error workflow (a per-workflow setting).
